root_motivation: A frontline social-services helper (rural clinic, mutual-aid site) needs an on-device, offline-capable resource directory to answer 'what services exist near here for this need' without reliable internet or budget for cloud APIs. The homeward ingest→normalize→query pattern is proven and directly reusable pointed at HSDS human-services data.
user_persona: A frontline helper (social worker, community health worker, mutual-aid volunteer) running the relay binary on a laptop or Raspberry Pi at a clinic, community centre, or pop-up site — possibly with no internet. They type 'relay directory query' to look up referrals during a client session.

acceptance_criteria.description: cargo build --release produces a relay binary; relay directory --help lists import, query, stats subcommands.
Importing a fixture HSDS-JSON export yields expected normalized Resource rows (golden test: known input → known schema output).
CSV ingestor parses a 211-style sheet into the same schema; malformed rows are skipped with a counted warning, never panic.
Dedup: two source records for the same org+service+location collapse to one Resource (deterministic, tested on fixture with known duplicates).
query --need food --near <lat,lon> --radius-km 10 returns only food resources within 10km, ordered by distance (golden test on seeded store).
Eligibility filtering: --eligibility under18 excludes resources whose eligibility flags exclude minors (tested on fixtures).
Store is durable: import, drop the process, re-open, query — rows persist.
SIGPIPE-safe (sigpipe::reset() in main) so relay directory query | head doesn't panic; strict clippy (unwrap/expect/panic = deny) clean.

scope: relay-directory lib crate: normalized Resource model (HSDS-aligned), Ingestor trait, HsdsJsonIngestor, CsvIngestor, dedup by org+service+location, SQLite store (rusqlite bundled), structured query builder with proximity + eligibility filtering
relay binary (relay-bin): directory import, directory query, directory stats subcommands
All operations offline-capable — no network calls in core path
Deterministic dedup using stable source-id hash
non_goals: No real-time sync with live 211 APIs or HSDS cloud endpoints (future crate)
No LLM-based need extraction in relay-directory itself (that is relay-match)
No user authentication, multi-tenant, or web service interface
No full HSDS taxonomy of 2000+ service codes — only the top-level categories needed for matching

additional.no_network_in_tests: all ACs are deterministic, no network or LLM required

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a local human-services resource directory?
five_whys_trace.a: A frontline helper can't refer someone to a service they can't find — current directories are scattered PDFs, county sites, and stale 211 spreadsheets.

five_whys_trace.q: Why local/on-device rather than querying a cloud API?
five_whys_trace.a: A rural clinic or pop-up mutual-aid site has no reliable internet and no cloud budget; the tool must work offline and free.

five_whys_trace.q: Why HSDS rather than a custom schema?
five_whys_trace.a: Open Referral's HSDS is the established interop standard for 211s and resource directories — real data exports exist to ingest rather than building a toy.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should relay-directory be a standalone crate or part of the relay workspace?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Part of the relay workspace (~/wintermute/relay) per the PRD — the relay binary hosts directory subcommands alongside future match/intake/letters commands.
